key_insight: The paper shows how zero-noise extrapolation can be adapted to indirect-control VQE by using a symmetry-based strategy for the one-dimensional XY spin chain, despite the challenge of constructing inverse operations for time-evolution dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This matters for quantum hardware because indirect control can reduce control-channel noise, and adding practical error mitigation can improve the reliability of near-term quantum simulation and optimization workflows.
method: Identify the ZNE obstacle in indirect-control circuits: continuous Hamiltonian evolution makes standard unitary folding hard to realize.
Relax the indirect-control constraint minimally and exploit XY-chain symmetry to create physically implementable noise amplification.
Use the adapted ZNE procedure to mitigate errors in indirect-control VQE.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a feasibility study rather than benchmark results, focusing on the construction and adaptation of ZNE for indirect-control VQE.
watch_item: The approach depends on a symmetry-specific setting and a minimal relaxation of indirect-control assumptions, so portability to other Hamiltonians or hardware models may be limited.
paper_title: Error Mitigation by Zero-Noise Extrapolation (ZNE) in Indirect-Control System
